{{Quote|The rebel spy has eluded the ''pursuit squads'', Governor Corwyth...shall I have the conveyor halted?''"''<br />''"''And cut off the ''ore flow'' to the planet's ''furnaces''...? Cause a temporary ''shut down''?! That would be doing the Alliance's work ''for'' them, you fool!|The radio officer and Governor Corwyth|<ref name="APL" />}}
A '''radio officer''' served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Metalorn/Legends|Metalorn]] during the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]. Alongside [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Corwyth]], the [[Comlink/Legends|radio]] [[Officer/Legends|officer]] oversaw the hunt for [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] when she infiltrated the planet in the name of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]. Using a [[Homing beacon|tracking device]] implemented in a [[Blaster rifle/Legends|blaster rifle]] Organa stole, the officer followed the princess' movements through one of Metalorn's [[Factory/Legends|factories]].

The hunt ultimately proved fruitless as Organa managed to use the Empire's [[weapons detection system]] against them by placing the stolen gun in an [[Cargo crawler|ore conveyor]] to throw off her pursuers. Corwyth tried to blame the failure in capturing Organa on the security system, but when the officer tried to reason that the system itself worked as intended, Corwyth throttled the officer by the collar.

==Biography==
===Infiltrator on Metalorn===
{{Quote|As long as we're monitoring the ''weapon''...she can't ''escape!'' Order out ''more units''...have them ''converge'' on the signal!|Governor Corwyth shouts out an order to his radio officers|<ref name="APL" />}}
[[File:Monitor_control.png|thumb|left|200px|The officer and his comrades monitored Metalorn from Monitor Control.]]
A [[Human/Legends|human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] served the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as a [[Subspace transceiver/Legends|radio]] [[Officer/Legends|officer]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Metalorn/Legends|Metalorn]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Serving under [[Governor/Legends|Governor]] [[Corwyth]], the officer worked from [[Monitor Control]], a communications hub that oversaw Metalorn's security. Due to a combination of Corwyth's [[information control program]] and the [[House of Tagge/Legends|House of Tagge]] [[weapons detection system]], the [[Factory/Legends|factory]] world's populace knew nothing of the Empire's war against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="APL" />

During the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">[[Star Wars (1977) 30|''Star Wars'' (1977) 30]] takes place after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' dates to [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], but before the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman Tagge]], which ''The New Essential Chronology'' dates to [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].</ref> monitor control was paid a visit by [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Orman Tagge/Legends|Orman Tagge]]. The visit happened to coincide with a [[Mission to Metalorn (Galactic Civil War)|rebel mission]] to infiltrate the planet and spread the seeds of rebellion.<ref name="APL" />

The infiltrator, [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], eventually stole an Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] [[Blaster rifle/Legends|rifle]], which triggered a [[condition red]]. [[Unidentified radio officer 2|Another officer]] reported the situation to Corwyth, who expressed outrage by the rebel attack. After the second officer got a bead on the [[Unidentified stormtrooper (Metalorn)|stormtrooper's]] stolen [[Rifle/Legends|rifle]], Corwyth sent troops in pursuit. The radio officer then monitored both the movement of the troops and the blaster. Meanwhile, the heightened activity in the area was passed off as a drill to the curious populace.<ref name="APL" />

===Duped===
{{Quote|How does the ''hunt'' progress?''"''<br />''"''The ''last unit'' is now in position in Smelter Bay Five, Governor Corwyth. And the ''monitor'' shows...the ore conveyor is speeding the rebel spy straight ''into'' their waiting guns!|Corwyth and the radio officer track Organa's blaster|<ref name="APL" />}}
[[File:Corwyth_is_mad.png|thumb|right|200px|Governor Corwyth blasted his frustrations about the Organa debacle at the radio officer.]]
The blaster's signal eventually made its way to an [[Cargo crawler|ore conveyor]], prompting the radio officer to ask if he should order the conveyor to halt. The request was angrily vetoed by Corwyth, who believed such an action would be in the Rebellion's favor. The radio officer, however, believed that Organa was intending to sabotage something. Eventually, a [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]] of soldiers had managed to reach the [[Smelter Bay Five|smelting bay]] ahead of the [[Blaster/Legends|blaster's]] signal in order to cut the princess off. Corwyth was pleased with the development, but in his state of concentration, he failed to notice Baron Tagge slip from the room. Meanwhile, the waiting unit's ambush proved unsuccessful: Organa had learned of the rifle's tracking device and had ditched the weapon in the [[Ore/Legends|ore]] conveyor.<ref name="APL" />

Furious, Corwyth grabbed the radio officer by the collar as he attempted to downplay Organa's escape as an unprecedented move of using the Empire's technology against them. Corwyth demanded additional units to find Organa. By then, however, Organa had already completed her mission and bested Tagge in a brief duel. Afterwards, she escaped the planet.<ref name="APL" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|In all ''fairness'', Governor...the system ''worked''. Who could anticipate the Alliance agent ''using'' it to decoy us after the blaster instead of ''her''?''"''<br />''"''Is that supposed to comfort ''me''?|The radio officer and Corwyth discuss Organa's tactics|<ref name="APL" />}}
The radio officer was a [[Color/Legends|light]]-skinned human with reddish-brown [[Hair/Legends|hair]] and blue [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. The officer dutifully followed the movements of Organa and Corwyth's men, and reported on the evolving incident as developments occurred. Corwyth derided the man as a fool, however, when the officer suggested a temporary halt to ore transportation in order to capture Organa.<ref name="APL" />

Nevertheless, when Corwyth tried to blame the failure to capture Organa based on the weapon tracking system on Tagge's security measures, the officer reasoned that the system had indeed worked as intended. Corwyth wanted nothing to do with the contradiction to his word, however, and throttled the hapless officer.<ref name="APL" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Who_the_hecc_is_talking.png|thumb|right|200px|Despite being drawn in conversation with Corwyth, the speech bubble is drawn coming from a nonspeaking character.]]
Created for the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[Star Wars (1977) 30|''Star Wars'' (1977) 30]], an issue of the [[Marvel Comics]] [[Star Wars (1977)|''Star Wars'']] series, the nameless radio officer played a supporting role in the story. ''A Princess Alone'' was written by [[Archie Goodwin]] and illustrated by [[Carmine Infantino]] and [[Gene Day]], and was released on [[December 30]], [[1979]].<ref name="APL" />

During one panel, the officer can be seen talking to Corwyth shortly before Corwyth angrily grabs the man. However, the speech bubble is drawn so that it emanates from an entirely different character. Given the sequence of events and action of the characters, this article treats the discrepancy as an illustrator's mistake.
